content:
alex: Quick ask — finance flagged an unexpected bump in cross-region egress & committed instance spend last month. Can we do a short region-by-region sensitivity that factors in reserved vs burst mix, NVLink-enabled instance premiums, and egress? Need rough recommendations for placement for inference pools (chat/embeddings) by EOD.

maria: I ran a quick head-to-head for SFO / ORD / LON / SIN on our steady traffic profile (p50 seq=64, p95 seq=512) — numbers from last 30d usage + list pricing + our commit discounts.

maria: summary table (hourly equivalent, normalized):
```
region, effective_gpu_hour_usd, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, typical_egress_per_hour_gb
sfo, 3.8, 28, 110, 12
ord, 3.5, 32, 130, 11
lon, 4.1, 30, 115, 9
sin, 3.2, 45, 160, 8
```

maria: notes: sin has cheaper base GPU but network latency to key customers increases p50/p95. lon egress cheaper if we keep traffic intra-eu, but committed discounts are smaller in our current contract.

jon: Where did you fold in NVLink/instance-premium? Some of our streaming chat fleets need NVLink for multi-GPU models else p95 explodes.

maria: NVLink premiums added as +0.6 usd effective per gpu-hour for multi-gpu placements. For chat (multi-gpu) we modeled that separately — if NVLink required, ord/sfo become relatively better due to lower cross-az variance.

alex: Good. Finance, what are the hard constraints on reservation flexibility? Raj — any appetite to shift commit dollars between regions? 

raj-finance: We have ~300k/mo reserve commitment for NA and 100k/mo for EU. Re-alloc requires 30d notice for most contracts; cloud marketplace items are ~90d. Possible but not immediate. Also egress discounts kick in only after volume thresholds (we're just below for EU).

tina-sre: Ops note — we saw occasional 20% CPU steal on SIN host pools during local maintenance windows which increased p95 for non-NVLink shards. If we move critical workloads to SIN for cost, need stronger isolation or dedicated capacity.

jon: Proposal: keep embeddings (single-gpu) in SIN + ORD mixed spot/reserved 60/40 to reduce cost for heavy batch workloads; keep chat (multi-gpu with NVLink) in SFO + ORD reserved-heavy for latency; use LON for EU-sensitive customers only, push traffic to LON if region tag matches to save egress.

alex: Can we simulate 30/60/10 commit split (NA/EU/APAC) and show delta to current snapshot? Maria — small sim should be quick.

maria: Running quick sim now. Assumptions: current mix NA70/EU20/APAC10, target 30/60/10, move 20% of reserved from NA->EU on 30d notice, keep APAC reserved same, increased spot in NA to cover variable. Results (monthly):
```
metric, baseline_usd, proposed_usd, delta_usd
infra_gpu_reserve, 420k, 360k, -60k
egress_net, 85k, 92k, +7k
total_estimated, 505k, 452k, -53k
```

maria: Caveats: this assumes we hit EU egress threshold within 6 weeks; if not, delta is -40k instead. Also perf-sensitive chat cost under proposed splits rises ~3% in latency-sensitive 95th due to slightly higher avg hop in APAC->NA traffic.

raj-finance: -53k is compelling but we need transition plan for 30d notice + capacity ramp. Also audit implications for Private customers — check data residency before moving.

alex: Action items:
- maria: produce a 7-day canary plan to move 10% of embeddings to SIN reserved/spot mix + observe p95 and egress delta (due in 24h)
- jon/tina-sre: test NVLink latency on ORD vs SFO with synthetic load (canary multi-gpu pod) and report differences (48h)
- raj-finance: confirm reallocation timeline & any penalties (24h)
- alex: I'll draft customer comms for any region-residency impacted customers if we decide to shift.

ops-bot: autoscaler:observed - triggered scale-up on embeddings-sin pool at 2025-10-14T14:23:10Z due to concurrent job surge. (link: https://console/redwood/autoscaler/events/9821)

maria: I'll kick off the sim & push results into the deck and include per-route latency impact. Will ping once the 7-day canary config is up in k8s (namespace infra-canary).

jon: If canary looks good and finance signs off, we should plan a staged re-reserve over two billing cycles to avoid penalties.

alex: Thanks — this is the direction. Keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
